title: Improve KV page reuse and reduce fragmentation for paged attention with prefetch-aware scheduling
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Background: The paged-attention path reduces peak memory but exposes KV page fragmentation and churn in the per-tenant KV cache. We have seen increased OOM/eviction storms for mixed short/long context workloads and measurable perf regressions when the runtime frequently allocates/deallocates small pages.

Problem statement: Reduce long-term fragmentation and improve KV page reuse across concurrent prefill/decode workloads while keeping prefill latency low. Ensure eviction policy prioritizes cheap-to-recompute entries and preserves hot prefixes.

Goals (acceptance criteria):
- Reduce average per-GPU KV memory fragmentation by >= 30% in mixed traffic (measured by free-contiguous-page ratio).
- Decrease number of concurrent eviction events per minute for a node by >= 40% under the mixed short/long traffic benchmark.
- No regression in 99th percentile prefill latency > 5% compared to baseline.
- Implementation should be controlled by flags and tunable at runtime for rollout.

Non-goals: full rewrite of allocator; changing model-format or introducing extra model-format compatibility layers.

Risks: compaction can stall decode if done synchronously; aggressive pinning can reduce effective cache capacity; instrumentation overhead.
design_options: Slab-backed allocator: allocate fixed-size slabs (e.g., 4KB/16KB/64KB) and fulfill page requests from slabs to reduce fragmentation. Pros: simple, predictable. Cons: internal fragmentation for small pages.

Generational allocator with hotset: track hot prefixes (by access frequency) and place them in a separate 'young' segment that is compacted less frequently. Pros: preserves hot prefixes; supports quick reuse. Cons: bookkeeping overhead.

Cost-aware eviction: when evicting choose pages by recompute cost estimate (tokens_to_recompute * compute_cost) instead of LRU. Pros: better trade-off between memory and CPU; avoids evicting cheap-to-recompute items. Cons: requires cost model and tuning.

Background compaction thread: asynchronously compact free extents to produce larger contiguous regions during low-load windows. Pros: reduces fragmentation without blocking decode. Cons: complexity and potential interference with GPU memory operations.

Prefetch-aware scheduling: during prefill schedule KV page allocations/prefetches in order that reduces scatter (group by slab) and prioritize allocations that can be satisfied from existing hot slabs. Pros: reduces cold allocations and tail latency. Cons: scheduling complexity across worker threads.
experiment_plan: Microbench harness: create synthetic mixed-traffic generator (short prompt 32 tokens: 200rps, long prompt 2048 tokens: 10rps) to reproduce fragmentation profile.
Implement slab allocator toggle behind runtime flag and run A/B benchmarks on a 4-GPU node with paged-attention enabled.
Measure metrics: contiguous_free_pages_ratio, eviction_events/min, prefill_p99_latency, tokens/sec, GPU_utilization, wall_time_compaction.
Run cost-aware eviction variant with a simple cost model (tokens_from_prefix, attention_layer_count) and compare memory vs recompute CPU overhead.
Canary rollout: enable slab + background compaction for 10% of hosted fleet for 48h with enhanced tracing; monitor OOMs, p99 latency, and eviction churn dashboard.
If compaction shows brief stalls, test incremental compaction with small work units and yield points tied to decode checkpoints.
decisions: 03-01-2025: Chosen initial approach: implement slab-backed allocator + cost-aware eviction + background compaction (async) behind runtime flags. Reason: best trade-off between implementation complexity and measurable fragmentation reduction.
03-02-2025: Will implement a simple recompute cost model first (tokens_to_regenerate * layer_multiplier) and iterate based on benchmarks.
comments: 2025-02-14 - Aisha Khan: Triage meeting notes: repeated eviction spikes observed on g4dn workloads; initial heap-dump shows many small free extents. Prioritize a quick-win (slab allocator) + longer-term compaction design.
2025-02-19 - Marco Ruiz (review): Questioned slab sizing defaults; suggested adaptive slab sizes based on observed page-size histogram. Action: add histogram collection to allocator metrics.
2025-02-25 - Taylor Chen: Prototype of slab allocator landed in feature branch. Initial microbench shows 22% improvement in contiguous_free_pages_ratio; eviction_events/min down 18% on synthetic mix.

2025-02-28 - SRE (Elena Park): Flagging concern: background compaction must not hold CUDA pin or block page-locked memory operations. Recommend ensuring compaction runs on CPU and signals GPU when safe.
2025-03-03 - Taylor Chen: Updated experiment plan with incremental compaction and prefetch-aware scheduler. Next: run cost-aware eviction variant and schedule canary with rollout guard.
